speaker: Doctor
text: That will help me understand your background. Given your history of gait and limb ataxia, have you noticed any changes in your handwriting, speech, or coordination over the past few years?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds concerning; has your speech become slurred or your handwriting become difficult to control as well? Additionally, have you experienced any unexplained weight loss, night sweats, or a history of tuberculosis?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. Given your history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab, combined with new-onset progressive ataxia, you must undergo an urgent MRI of the brain to confirm this diagnosis.
